decision.why: Three cuts of one real talk: the edit technique ingests it once (the silence map, the transcript), then one timeline per pick — three parallel outputs of the same pipeline, each a different strongest moment. The reframe keeps the speaker framed in 9:16 and the captions ride the transcript.

alternatives.rejected_because: the talk is real footage — motion cannot use it
the simplest thing that could work — but the ask says three, and three is exactly the same pipeline run three times on different picks

segments.role: the three cuts (one pipeline, three picks)
segments.brief: Ingest the talk once; pick the three strongest distinct moments from the transcript (the hooks, the payoff, the closer); cut each to 45 seconds with the same caption design and the same reframe rule; ship three vertical timelines.
acceptance: three complete thoughts, three different hooks
the same caption design across the three
the speaker framed in 9:16 in all three
three separate highlights (the count is three: three 45-second vertical pieces)
the three highlights cover different moments — three hooks, not one moment thrice
each is cut tight: pauses, silence and filler out
the talk's own speech is carried (the speaker's audio, not a bed over mute)
the selection targets the talk's strongest moments (measured from the transcript)
